headline: Ansar Allah claim six operations against Saudi targets incl. Aramco Khurais and Riyadh airport, as retaliation for the Nov 6 Taiz
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the statement was made] Saree announced six operations with ballistic/cruise missiles and drones, framed explicitly as retaliation for the Saudi attack on al-Hadara market, Taiz (Nov 6, 30 killed) and the Bani Hushaysh residential strikes near Sanaa (Nov 7, 25 killed, recorded…
sources: Yahya Saree, spokesman for the Yemeni Armed Forces (Ansar Allah), televised/X statement, Nov 7; reported by AFP via Dawn and by Al Mayadeen
fault_line: Did the Ansar Allah actually hit Aramco Khurais and Riyadh airport -- or is this a retaliation claim with no proven damage? And: does Saudi air defence hold, or is the shield failing?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the statement was made] Saree announced six operations with ballistic/cruise missiles and drones, framed explicitly as retaliation for the Saudi attack on al-Hadara market, Taiz (Nov 6, 30 killed) and the Bani Hushaysh residential strikes near Sanaa (Nov 7, 25 killed, recorded 1900-03): (1) Riyadh -- King Khalid International Airport, Aramco oil storage tanks and an Aramco distillation tower; (2) Khurais -- Aramco facilities; (3) Pumping Station No. 8, al-Dawadmi; (4) Saudi National Guard camp, Najran, claimed direct hit with many dead/wounded; (5) Saudi forces east of al-Jawf over three phases, dozens killed/wounded; (6) Saudi forces east of Raghwan and Medghal, Marib. Saree said each operation 'successfully achieved its objective'. [ALLEGATION -- hits/damage/casualties] No independent confirmation of any hit, damage or casualty; Saudi Arabia/coalition have not confirmed any of the six; no imagery or debris published. [CONTEXT -- partially consistent, does not confirm] The coalition DID intercept and destroy a Ansar Allah cruise missile toward the Riyadh region on Saturday Nov 7 (recorded 1600-01), and a drone was intercepted late Nov 6 (0700-03) -- consistent with at least one Riyadh-bound launch, but it does not confirm six operations or any successful hit. [NOT THE OCT 30 CLAIM] A different Saree 'six attacks' claim circulated Oct 30 (Ras Tanura, Abqaiq, Rabigh, King Fahd Airport Dammam, Najran command centre -- flagged as re-date trap at 0700-05(g)); today's target list (Khurais, Pumping Station 8, al-Jawf, Raghwan/Medghal) is different and the stated retaliation motive ties to Nov 6-7 events. The Saree statement video itself is dated 7/11/2026 (social search, IG reel). [ENERGY CONTEXT] Brent was near $116 on Friday per DailyGraph (Brent $115.74, +0.75%), with traders citing Ansar Allah attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure; treat as market context, not a verified price print from this scan.
sections.what_verified: Statement confirmed by 2 distinct publisher families (AFP T1 + Iran International T3); Al Mayadeen carries the same statement but has NO declared tier in the registry so it does not count. Hits/damage: 0 families -- no independent confirmation.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Arabia/coalition have issued no confirmation of any of the six claimed strikes; the coalition's only Nov 7 statement is the Riyadh cruise-missile intercept (1600-01). The Oct 30 Saree six-attacks claim (different targets) shows Saree reuses the 'six operations' framing -- past claims do not prove today's, but they warn against treating the count as evidence of six successful hits. No flight-tracking, satellite or Aramco statement corroborates damage at Khurais or Riyadh airport.
sections.why_matters: Ansar Allah answer the Sanaa toll of 25 with six claimed strikes on Saudi oil and airports -- but no proof of a single hit. Khurais is the new name: Aramco's desert heartland, named as a target for the first time in this round.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Dawn liveblog entry 09:28pm PKT = 20:28 , AFP; Al Mayadeen same evening) -- Ansar Allah claim six operations against Saudi targets incl. Aramco Khurais and Riyadh airport, as retaliation for the Nov 6 Taiz market strike and Nov 7 Sanaa strikes

totw_analysis: Our read: Ansar Allah answer the Sanaa toll of 25 with six claimed strikes on Saudi oil and airports -- but no proof of a single hit. Khurais is the new name: Aramco's desert heartland, named as a target for the first time in this round. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did the Ansar Allah actually hit Aramco Khurais and Riyadh airport -- or is this a retaliation claim with no proven damage? And: does Saudi air defence hold, or is the shield failing?
